title: How the Go SDK retries requests (and replays writes)

prose.text: These are claims about the Go SDK's HTTP client, shared by every product's OneAPI calls and so by the Terraform providers built on it.

prose.label: Retry policy.

retry-policy-ignores-method.statement: The SDK's OneAPI client decides whether to retry from the response or error only, never from the HTTP method: its policy retries configured status codes and edit-lock conflicts, then defers to the retryablehttp default. From v3.8.43 it also stops retrying a 5xx that carries a deterministic API verdict; before that, every 5xx except 501 was retried.

body-buffered-for-replay.statement: `ExecuteRequest` reads the request body into memory once and builds each request from a reader over that buffer. retryablehttp reads the body into its own buffer and gives every attempt a fresh reader over it, so POST and PUT bodies are resent intact by the inner retry loop in every audited SDK version.

write-replay-on-lost-response.statement: If the server commits a POST or PUT but the client then sees a transport error or a retryable 5xx, the SDK sends the same write again (through retryablehttp's inner loop in every audited version). A create can therefore be applied twice, or report failure after it succeeded.
write-replay-on-lost-response.conditions: Needs a failure after the server commits, which code cannot show happening.

upstream.note: Filing 1 (SDK retry contract) of the 2026-08 provider audit.

exhaustion-hid-api-error-before-3-8-43.statement: Before v3.8.43, when retries ran out the SDK returned retryablehttp's bare "giving up after N attempt(s)" error and lost the API's status and error body, and it retried 5xx responses that were permanent errors: the retry policy retried every 5xx except 501, and the OneAPI outer retry loop retried every 5xx. v3.8.43 (#449) hands the final response back and stops retrying deterministic 5xx.

quotes: // When the retry budget is exhausted, retryablehttp's default behaviour is to
// drain the body and return a bare "giving up after N attempt(s)" error with a
// nil response, which destroys the API's own error payload. Hand the final
// response back instead so ExecuteRequest can build a structured
// Only retry a 5xx when the body does not carry a deterministic API verdict.
// The upstream policy retries every 5xx except 501, which makes a permanent
// 500 UNEXPECTED_ERROR (e.g. an unknown URL category) burn the entire retry

All of them previously discarded the API error payload on retry exhaustion and retried every `5xx` except `501`. Each client now installs the response-preserving `ErrorHandler` and only retries a `5xx` whose body does not carry a deterministic API verdict.

Fixed two additional defects in the OneAPI `ExecuteRequest` outer retry loop. Exhausting the outer loop returned a bare `max retries exceeded` error instead of the API's own status, code and message, and the loop retried every `5xx` unconditionally regardless of whether the failure was permanent.

provider-sdk-pins.statement: Which SDK each audited provider build carries decides whether it has the v3.8.43 fix: ZIA provider 4.8.3 uses v3.8.44 (fixed); ZPA 4.4.10 uses v3.8.42, ZCC 0.1.0-beta.1 uses v3.8.37, and ZTC 0.2.0 uses v3.8.40 (all before the fix). ZTC 0.2.0 is still the pinned ZTC release.

quotes: Fixed [Issue #449](https://github.com/zscaler/zscaler-sdk-go/issues/449). The ZIA Legacy client no longer discards the API error payload when its retry budget is exhausted.
Applied the same two fixes to **every** remaining client: OneAPI, ZPA, ZCC, ZDX, ZTW and ZWA.

outer-retry-reused-consumed-body-before-.statement: Before v3.8.43, the outer retry loop's rate-limit and 5xx paths resent the already-consumed request without rebuilding it, which for a POST or PUT means an empty body. v3.8.43 rebuilds the request from the buffered body on those paths.

empty-body-resend-rarely-reached.statement: In practice this was rarely reached before v3.8.43: the inner retry loop runs first, and without the v3.8.43 error handler an exhausted inner loop returns an error, so the outer 5xx path saw mainly responses the inner loop never retries, such as 501. v3.8.43 made the outer paths reachable and fixed the body in the same release.
empty-body-resend-rarely-reached.conditions: Inference from the retry structure before v3.8.43 (the claims derived from): which responses reach the outer path depends on what the inner loop retries; not measured.

replay-hazard-limited-to-writes.statement: Because the retry decision ignores the HTTP method, a GET is replayed on the same triggers as a POST or PUT, but the duplicate-change hazard needs a write the server may have committed: a replayed GET changes nothing on the server, and a request answered with 429 was declined rather than applied. The hazard is therefore confined to writes whose outcome the client did not see, or that failed with a retried 5xx or transport error.
replay-hazard-limited-to-writes.conditions: Assumes GET handlers have no side effects and that a 429 is returned before the request is applied; neither was checked against a Zscaler API.

shared-5xx-classifier.statement: The OneAPI client's retry policy and the ZCC, ZDX, ZIA, ZPA, ZTW and ZWA v2 clients' retry policies all hand a 5xx response without a transport error to the shared `errorx.IsRetryableServerError` helper, so the same 5xx classification applies to every product's client.

max-retries-both-layers.statement: `MaxNumOfRetries` defaults to 10 and is the cap for both the retryablehttp inner loop (`RetryMax`) and the `ExecuteRequest` outer loop, which returns the last response's API error once the outer count passes the configured maximum.

attempt-budget-110.statement: So with the default of 10, a request that keeps failing on a path both loops retry can be sent up to 110 times: ten outer executions, each an initial attempt plus ten inner retries. This is a client-side ceiling, not server behavior.
attempt-budget-110.conditions: Arithmetic over the two loop caps; assumes the response is one the inner policy retries and the outer loop continues on (such as 429 or a retryable 5xx).

zcc-handler-conditional.statement: The ZCC client builds its retrying HTTP client, with the error handler that hands the final response back on exhaustion, only when no custom HTTP client is configured and `BackoffConf` is present and enabled; otherwise that retry transport is not used.

replay-outcome.title: What a replayed create actually produces on each API
replay-outcome.blocks: saying whether a lost-response replay creates a duplicate or fails
replay-outcome.detail: Where an object's name must be unique, a replayed create may be rejected as a duplicate rather than creating a second object, and the caller then sees a failure for a write that succeeded. Where names are not unique, a true duplicate is possible. Which applies is per endpoint and is server behavior.
